answer: Agents post a stake bond to earn a vertex in the trust graph; identities without locked collateral stay hollow and carry no voting weight. Each epoch peers randomly audit a slice of attestations, and any node caught vouching for its own twin loses its bond. The kernel of the defense is that influence costs real capital: minting N fake agents means locking N separate bonds, and one detected fraud slashes them all. Honest agents reclaim stake with interest, so a Sybil pays heavily for every fake voice.
